content: Pyrethrin combined with piperonyl butoxide is a medication designed to eliminate parasites and their eggs. It is specifically used to treat infestations such as scabies, which is a skin condition caused by mites, as well as lice infestations affecting the head, body, or pubic area (commonly referred to as crabs). However, it is important to note that this medication does not prevent future infestations. This medication is available in liquid, gel, and shampoo forms. Typically, a single application is sufficient to treat the infestation. However, if live parasites reappear, the treatment may need to be repeated after one week. In such cases, it is essential to contact your doctor. Always follow the instructions provided on the package or prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the medication exactly as directed, and do not apply more or less than prescribed or use it more frequently than instructed. If you have open cuts or scratches on your hands, wear rubber gloves while applying the medication. If the medication accidentally comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water for at least five minutes. When using the liquid or gel form, follow these steps: 1. Apply enough medication to cover the affected hairy area and the surrounding regions. If you are unsure where to apply it, consult your doctor or pharmacist. 2. Leave the medication on for exactly 10 minutes. 3. Wash the treated area thoroughly with warm water and soap or regular shampoo. 4. Dry the area with a clean towel. 5. Wash your hands to remove any residual medication. 6. Change into clean clothes. When using the shampoo form, follow these steps: 1. Shake the shampoo bottle well before use. Apply the shampoo to dry hair and scalp or skin, ensuring complete coverage. 2. Add a small amount of water to work the shampoo into a lather. 3. Leave the shampoo on for exactly 10 minutes. 4. Rinse your hair thoroughly with water. 5. Dry your hair with a clean towel. 6. Use a fine-tooth comb to remove nits (lice eggs and larvae). 7. Wash your hands to remove any residual medication. If you are treating head lice, clean combs and brushes by washing them with the liquid, gel, or shampoo, and rinse them thoroughly with water to remove the medication. Before using pyrethrin and piperonyl butoxide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to pyrethrin, piperonyl butoxide, ragweed, petroleum products, or any other medications. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Pregnant individuals should wear gloves when applying this medication to another person to prevent absorption through the skin. This medication may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Skin irritation Rash Redness Swelling Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Pyrethrin and piperonyl butoxide are intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest the medication. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. After using this medication, machine-wash or dry-clean all clothing, bed linens, and towels used in the past two days. Use hot water and dry items in a hot dryer for at least 20 minutes. Thoroughly clean all bathtubs, showers, and toilets in your home with rubbing alcohol. If you have transmitted the parasites to family members or close contacts (including sexual partners), advise them to consult a doctor if they develop symptoms of infestation. For individuals with scabies, itching may persist for several weeks after treatment due to skin sensitivity to the parasites. This does not indicate treatment failure. Contact your doctor if you have any concerns or questions. Do not share your medication with others. If you have any questions about pyrethrin and piperonyl butoxide, consult your pharmacist.
